quand il dit en y auoir aucuns chaſtrez, qui ſont ainſi
nez du ventre de leurs meres: & d'autres qui ont eſté
chaſtrez par les hommes: & quelques vns, qui ſe ſont
eux meſmes chaſtrez pour le royaume des cieux {y}. Car
l'Euangeliſte (duquel le deſſeing eſt autre que le but de
noſtre diſcours) veut dire, que ceux qui ſont chaſtrez
de nature, ou par force des hommes, ſ'ils ſont chaſtes
& continens, n'en doyuent rapporter grande louange,
d'autant que leur chaſteté procede plus de cõtrainte &
neceſſité, que d'honneſte affection & vertu Chreſtiẽne.
mais ceux qui ſe ſont chaſtrez eux meſmes, non point

uncertain.note: the margin note keyed p (first note on the page, beside body lines 1-5) has no visible marker p anywhere in the body. Every body line of the page was examined at 2.5x full width and the first seven lines again at 3.5-7x with contrast raised; no italic letter stands between words on lines 1-8, and the first marker printed is {q} on line 8. Recorded per §4 as a note whose marker is missing: either the compositor omitted the marker letter or it failed to print. The alphabet is otherwise continuous from p041 (which ends at {o}) through q r ſ t u x y on this page.

The same word is set with a true ſſ ligature on lines[8] ('auſſi propre') and lines[20] ('aucuns auſſi le facent'), where both glyphs ascend. Transcribed as printed in each place, per §2.

uncertain.note: the mark over the second e of 'ſemẽce' is narrower and more angled than the broad flat tildes of 'naturellemẽt' on the same line, so it could be read as a circumflex. Read as a tilde: 'ſemence' contracted to 'ſemẽce' is the word, and the print has no circumflex elsewhere on the page.

uncertain.note: sic: 'ſe rrouue' for 'ſe trouue'. At 4x the first letter after the space is a clean r (vertical stem with a shoulder flag at x-height, no crossbar and no bottom curve), not a t that has lost its bar. Transcribed as printed.

uncertain.note: the point after the marker {u} is very lightly inked — a small round dot on the baseline, much fainter than the point after {t} on lines[15] or after {x} on lines[21]. Read as a period (the construction '. &' recurs on this page and on p041); a reader could take it for a speck and print 'coupé {u} & bien que'.

uncertain.note: the marker read as {u} is an italic glyph of two strokes that can look like an x at reading size. Confirmed as u at 12x by shape match with the key letter printed at the head of margin note u ('u l ſi ſeruus'), and distinct from the true italic x (crossing diagonals) printed both as the marker on lines[21] and as the key of margin note x. Sequence t (lines[15]) → u → x (lines[21]) agrees.

uncertain.text: neceſſité, que d'honneſte affection & vertu Chreſtiẽne.
uncertain.note: the mark over the e of 'Chreſtiẽne' is a flat horizontal wavy bar, i.e. a tilde for the omitted n ('Chreſtienne'), not the slanted acute the print uses on 'chaſtré', 'preallegué', 'chaſteté'. Read at 5x; a reader could write 'Chreſtiéne'.

the line-end mark after 'nou' is a round dot sitting on the baseline, not the raised short stroke the print uses for its hyphens (compare 'cõſultatio-', 'fraterni-', 'adil. e-', 'xxx-', 'ſic-' in these same notes). Transcribed as a point although the word continues 'uelles' on the next line; it may be a broken or badly inked hyphen.

the numeral is read as 'iij' (three minims, three dots, the last with a j descender) at 14x. 'iiij' cannot be wholly excluded on this impression, and the same Novel is cited on p041 (note b) as 'col iiij.'; the Novellae de nuptiis do stand in collatio iiij, so the sense favours iiij while the glyphs favour iij.

the print sets 'Gal.auxv.' with no space inside, so the word division is the reader's: 'au xv.' (Galen, book 15 of De usu partium — the next lines read 'li. de vſu. par|tium.') rather than 'aux v.'. §9 of the conventions shows the same formula set 'au xv. liur. de'.
no hyphen is printed at the line end although the word continues 'tium.' on the next line; transcribed as printed per §1.
sic: 'quaritur' for 'quæritur'. At 4x the letter after 'qu' is a single round a with no e joined to it; there is no æ ligature.
a small faint round dot stands between 'lege' and 'P'; read as a point, though it is lighter than the point after 'P' in the same line and could be a speck ('l. lege P. ſi').

the line opens 'ual' (u-a-l, clear at 9x) continuing 'ſi' from the previous line; 'ſi ual' does not resolve into a citation I can identify (D. ad legem Corneliam de ſicariis is plainly the title). A very faint speck follows 'ual' which may be a point; it is not transcribed. Nothing here is a guess — the letters are read as printed.
